# Keystone — Glossary / Nonprofit Jargon

- **Restricted funds** — gifts/grants a donor has designated for a specific program or purpose;
  can't be spent on anything else.
- **Unrestricted funds** — money the org can direct freely (general operating); the most flexible
  and hardest to raise.
- **Form 990** — the annual IRS information return every 501(c)(3) files; public document.
- **LOI** — Letter of Inquiry; the short pre-proposal a funder asks for before inviting a full
  grant proposal.
- **Match / matching gift** — a commitment (often from a major donor or corporation) to match
  other gifts dollar-for-dollar up to a cap, used to spur giving.
- **Cohort** — a group of students moving through a program together (e.g. the Bright Futures
  [Fall](../projects/bright-futures-fall.md) and [Spring](../projects/bright-futures-spring.md)
  cohorts).
- **Cultivation** — the process of building a relationship with a prospective donor before an ask.
- **Stewardship** — how you thank and retain a donor after a gift (reports, recognition, updates).
- **Naming gift / naming rights** — a major gift given in exchange for naming a program, space, or
  building after the donor (or someone they choose).
- **Development** — the fundraising function (Keystone's is led by
  [Daniela Cruz](../people/daniela-cruz.md)).
- **Program Officer (PO)** — a foundation's staff contact who manages the grant relationship
  (Hearthstone's is [Diane Alcott](../people/diane-alcott.md)).
- **Willow** — code name for a confidential board matter; use the code name only.
